utterances.text: So we do have staff there.

utterances.speaker: Sonia Russell
utterances.text: And again, it's through meetings with the program director as well as ICL leadership that attributes to where they are now.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm looking forward to hearing from ICL, and I certainly appreciate the work they're doing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Were the reporting standards and definitions identical in both years?

utterances.speaker: Sonia Russell
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they were.

chapters.summary: Morano notes 231 capacity but only 168 residents and asks why 63 beds are empty; Dalton says 198 are filled as of today, DHS is moving veterans from other shelters, and seven units are offline due to tarps.
chapters.title: Morano questions Dalton on empty beds at BAVR

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Last question I'll ask for now.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I have a number of other questions, but I know my colleagues do as well.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Your testimony says that Borden Avenue has capacity for 231 residents, but only 168 were living there as of last week.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: That means approximately 63 beds were unoccupied.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: At a time when hundreds of veterans are experiencing homelessness in New York City, why are so many beds empty?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Is that 63 more beds that could be used to make sure veterans are not sleeping on the street?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yeah, no, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I'll start and then I'll let the deputy commissioner add.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Actually, as of today, there are 198 beds filled.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We've been working, DHS, the deputy commissioner and others, have been working hard to move veterans from other shelters into the residence at Borden now that we control that eligibility entirely and expect to

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: continue to make transfers up into the space that the capacity allows for, acknowledging that there are seven units offline because of the tarps.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So we have moved with speed to fill the facility since the grant ended, and we'll have that facility up to the full census quickly.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So in terms of beds that are unavailable because of roof leaks or repairs, it's about seven?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Seven is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I have a number of other questions, but I'll defer to Chair Hudson and my colleagues.

chapters.summary: Hudson asks for the timeline on the long-term shelter capacity plan and safe haven sites; Dalton says a homelessness plan is forthcoming within a year and the city is not actively considering new sites until then.
chapters.title: Hudson questions Dalton on street homelessness and safe haven plan

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Murano.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: A few questions.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Questions I'd like to veer towards street homelessness and safe havens.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I understand that although we're nearly one year into this new administration, DHS is not actively considering new locations for street homeless sites, such as safe havens and drop-in centers, until the administration releases a long-term shelter capacity plan.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: What's the timeline for release of that plan so that we can continue long-term efforts to address street homelessness?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Thank you for that question.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And street homelessness and our unsheltered New Yorkers are my top priority.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And I would not say that we are not actively looking at bringing on additional safe haven beds.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But you are correct.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We have in the block by block report, we announced that there would be a homelessness plan within the next year.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And we are working on that homelessness plan, which would include, of course, a plan for our unsheltered neighbors.

chapters.summary: Hudson asks if the administration will support the nonprofit ownership model and appropriate funds for new street homeless sites; Dalton says all of that will be covered in the forthcoming homelessness plan.
chapters.title: Hudson asks Dalton about nonprofit ownership model and funding

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And does the administration plan to continue supporting the nonprofit ownership model as a tool for creating long-term shelter and safe haven capacity?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: All of that, too, will be covered in the homelessness plan, which we are working intently on right now.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay, I'm going to guess your answer to this, but will you commit to appropriate funds to that program to ensure the creation of new street homeless sites?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: All of those conversations are happening.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Again, really critical priority for me as I come to the city to make sure we're doing the most we can for our unsheltered New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It's a huge emphasis, a place where I've spent a lot of my time since I've been here and working on the plan that is forthcoming.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: We'll revisit that one.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Maybe better appropriate.

chapters.summary: Hudson asks if OMB cost concerns delayed or denied street homeless sites; Dalton says she knows of no such delays, is working with OMB on the plan, and does not know if OMB has visited shelters.
chapters.title: Hudson questions Dalton on OMB concerns and site delays

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Have any proposed street homeless sites been delayed or denied because of Office of Management and Budget concerns surrounding costs?

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And if so, what are those concerns and how has OMB determined which approaches to street homeless site funding offers the best long-term value for taxpayers?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: No, I do not know of any sites that are delayed for those reasons.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We are working on a forward-looking plan and working in partnership with OMB on that.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: They are certainly one voice in that conversation as well.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We have opinions about the best ways to serve this group of people.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: To your knowledge, has anyone from OMB visited?

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Any shelters in the network?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I think you would have to ask OMB.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Hudson asks for a 30-day written update on the shelter capacity plan, nonprofit ownership, and barriers to safe haven projects; Dalton commits to an update on status but not the plan itself.
chapters.title: Hudson requests written update on shelter capacity plan

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And can you commit to providing the committee within 30 days a written update identifying the status of the shelter capacity plan, the future of the nonprofit ownership program, and any policy or budget barriers

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: currently preventing new safe haven and drop-in center projects from advancing?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: An update?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I think an update we could provide, for sure.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: That was the question, right?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: A written update, yes.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: A written update on the status and all of these.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: On the status.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: In 30 days.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So from my perspective, just to make sure I can really agree to that.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Well, if you say it's a go, then staff has got to do it.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I am not committing to a homelessness plan or any of those in the next 30 days, but I would be happy to commit to an update on where we are with all of it.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Update on status.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Yeah, I also want to acknowledge Councilmember Juan and Councilmember Gutierrez who are here.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And then I think Councilmember Juan was first up in the queue.

chapters.summary: Won says she represents the only veteran shelter, calls communal showers inhumane, and notes partitions are promised in six to eight weeks; she then asks how many beds are offline due to leaks, and Dalton says seven, with Won noting they will be offline for two years minimum.
chapters.title: Won questions Dalton on Borden showers, roof leaks, and offline beds

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Marano.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you to all the agencies that have come to testify.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: It's so good to see you all.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: My name is Julie Wan.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: I'm currently the city council member representing the only veteran shelter in the entire city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: For the last five years, we have had the same amount of complaints.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And even before I was elected, we had the same amount of complaints, and it's extremely disturbing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: In addition, I saw, I appreciate your testimony where you address some of the concerns that we have heard for years about this shelter.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So as you have seen in the news, we've had a lot of shelter residents complain about the lack of privacy in the bathrooms.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Currently in the only veteran shelter, year after year for over 10 years, people have complained that they have to shower communally.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Could you imagine if you have served in war and now they want you to be butt naked in front of each other every time you want to shower?

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: That is currently what the system is and people have complained for years and every single year we have had lip service that there would be partitions put up, that there would be partitions put up, that there would be partitions put up.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And especially those who are struggling with mental illness, substance abuse, they're forced to either not shower.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Or shower in nudity in front of each other.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: That is no way to treat a human being with dignity.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: That is inhumane.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And I see in the testimony that there is a commitment to have partitions put up within the next six to eight weeks.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So we will continue to follow up with our shelter residents who want to have privacy and decency so that they can shower with dignity.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So we will wait for the next two months, starting from today, to make sure that finally that they will have privacy to shower.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Next, we have physically.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: seen and the press has seen how there is an incredible amount of leakage from the roof.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So I see that there's a commitment to make sure that there is some sort of roof and skylight replacement.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And it says that it's going to be from 2027 to 2029.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So could you help me understand how many beds are offline because of

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: the lack of capital repairs that were needed because it says that those who are affected by the leak will not be able to stay there and they will stay offline.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: How many beds are we talking about and the only shelter that we have in the city?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Thank you for that question, and I share the concern.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: and your approach to the requirement of privacy for our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So I do apologize on behalf of all of those veterans that those partitions had not been in place for so long, but we in this administration

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: saw that and are committed to working with ICL to get that done.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And I know you all will hold us accountable to do that over the timeline we proposed.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So right now, we have a vendor who is consistently assessing and making roof repairs.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And then we have tarps where we cannot patch those repairs.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And there is some water coming into the facility.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: There are seven tarps as of right now, and we monitor that on a very regular basis and will continue to do so until the roof and skylight repair is complete.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: As we proceed with the construction, we can keep the council updated, and we will do everything in our control to have minimal disruption to the facility.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: My understanding, and we can get back to you and make sure that this is correct, it's really only the replacement of the skylights that would take any units offline, which we can do in a

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: kind of staged way, such that we would not have a significant number of...

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: units offline.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so we can come back as the construction begins and give updates on that.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But I don't think we expect significant disruption while we replace the roof.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So how many beds are affected by the leak?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: There are seven beds affected by the leak right now.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And that means that there are not veterans.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Those beds are offline.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And those seven beds will be offline for two years minimum.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Can you also help me understand?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And that may be correct, but we also are making regular repairs.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so I think like sometimes it's five and sometimes it's seven.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And, you know, like it goes up and down a little bit as we make repairs to a roof that clearly needs to be replaced.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Can you help me understand?

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Is this the same contractor that has had this contract for this capital repair in the previous years?

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Or is this a new contractor?

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Who's responsible?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I believe we're just actually moving into procurement.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And I'll see if the deputy commissioner knows.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But I think, and we can make sure to get back to you, I think it is a different, we don't know who the vendor will be yet, I think, for the roof repair and for the full roof replacement.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so I don't think we could actually answer the question of whether there's a different contract.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Can I have more time, please?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: One more, please, and then we'll come back to you, just because we have a lot of our colleagues that want to.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Understood.

chapters.summary: Won says residents report mistreatment by ICL staff, lack of substance abuse and mental health services, and mandatory NDAs for elected officials; she thanks Dalton for speaking directly with veterans.
chapters.title: Won raises ICL mistreatment, NDAs, and service gaps

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So since I'm going to run out of time because I have to go vote, I may come back.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: I just want to put it on record that we have had clear complaints, multiple complaints directly.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: to the press on record as well as off record from constituents who live in the veteran shelter about the mistreatment of the people who live there

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: by the ICL employees themselves in negligence, that they're not receiving the

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: substance abuse services that they need, as well as mental health care, as well as caseworkers to help them

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: apply for permanent housing and also for mediation between conflict amongst the residents themselves.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And it's extremely concerning for them to send us direct messages and screenshots of ICL telling them that you're visiting that day and to clear all of their urine out of their individual rooms because they tend to urinate in their own

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: cupboards.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Because they don't have enough privacy in the bathrooms and they don't feel safe.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And also we have multiple instances of recordings and photographs of people who are continuing to have severe substance abuse within the shelter itself.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: We're extremely concerned, and we also want to hear a clear understanding and an update on the NDAs that are mandatory for elected officials to sign in order to enter the shelter.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: We can't have oversight authority over the shelter and city agencies if we have to sign an NDA and we cannot publicly speak about the issues that people are coming to us to complain about.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So I want to have that cleared up because I really appreciated you coming and speaking with the veterans themselves directly because they were.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: They were so sure that you were just going to walk away from them and not even look them in the eye, and you did the opposite.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: You were willing to speak to them, and you are willing to address these issues, so I very much appreciate you, and I look forward to working together to make sure that a lot of these issues are resolved.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Councilmember Palladino.

chapters.summary: Paladino asks Dalton how long she has been commissioner and about her prior experience, says she seems like a deer in headlights, and raises many concerns about Borden Avenue.
chapters.title: Paladino questions Dalton on experience and Borden concerns

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Let me commend my colleague, Julie Wan.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: That was excellent, Julie.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: You nailed it.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I'm interested in the Commissioner of Department of Social Services.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I believe your name is Erin Dalton.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: How long have you been commissioner for the Department of Social Services?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Since March 2nd.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: So you're a newbie.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: What was your prior experience before doing this?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I ran the Department of Human Services in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: That's Pittsburgh.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: There, my portfolio was broader than it is here.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I ran everything from newborn, early intervention, child protection, the mental health and substance use programs, the homelessness programs.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I also ran veteran services.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I ran aging programs and so violence prevention programs, a wide range of.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Okay, because obviously.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: It sounds like you're stuck like a deer in the headlights right now.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: We have many, many, many concerns.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: about the Borden Street shelter, most of which was eloquently put in front of you today.

chapters.summary: Paladino asks the cost to fix the roof; Dalton says $4.3 million for the entire roof and skylights, and Paladino asks about square footage and roof layers, which Dalton does not know.
chapters.title: Paladino questions roof cost and facility size

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Also, the Commissioner of Homeless Services.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: We have got, you're talking about how much is it going to cost?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: The number went by me.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Maybe it got caught in my head and I'm not quite sure, but I'd like you to repeat yourself.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: What is the amount to fix the roof that only is going to displace seven veterans?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: So that's a rather small piece of a roof unless you're doing the entire roof.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: What is the price of that?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I'll answer the question first about the price and then try to clarify the seven quickly.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Well, you...

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So the price that is budgeted is $4.3 million.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: $4.3 million.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: To replace the entire roof and skylights.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Are they removing just the third roof, the second roof?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: What's going on?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: You know there's three roofs, and then they've got to rip off and do a complete redo.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: How big is the facility?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: What's the square footage of the facility?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I'd have to get back to you.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: You're not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Because that determines price.

chapters.summary: Paladino compares $1.86 billion for migrants to veterans' subhuman conditions, demands 990s from nonprofits, criticizes NDAs, and says she is embarrassed and will keep pressure on the administration.
chapters.title: Paladino criticizes spending priorities and demands nonprofit 990s

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Other thing.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: We have now put aside $1.86 billion to house illegal immigrants in this country.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: $1.86 billion.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Billion dollars so that they

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: You go into hotels, have private bathrooms, kitchenettes, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: And our veterans are going to live in subhuman conditions.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: It's pathetic.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: What I heard here today is making me sick.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: There is absolutely zero reason for this to happen.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Also, we've got non-for-profits financing this.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I want the 990s on these non-for-profits.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I want to know who they are.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I want to see how much money these non-for-profits are making off of one shelter, homeless shelter, for our veterans, our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: This is absolutely disgusting and disgraceful.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I'm embarrassed for all of you.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: And when Julie went down there and visited with Phil, and they saw what they saw, and they had to send an NDA?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Ludicrous.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: As elected officials, we owe it to our fellow citizens, homeless, veterans, whatever, to know what's going on.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: The other thing is to not have mental health facilities set up for our veterans inside of these homeless shelters is also another disgrace.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: There are so many layers to this cake.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: How everybody's very calm here is wonderful, and I applaud you all.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: But let me tell you something.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Pull your act together.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Because going forward, we are going to be breathing all over you.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Wasteful spending, $1.86 billion going to illegals instead of to our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: And you're going to pay $4.3 million to fix a roof and displace seven veterans?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: We're supposed to be happy about that.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Proud of you for doing that.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I'm not proud of you.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I'm embarrassed for you.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Our veterans deserve top-notch treatment.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: And that's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I got a press conference to do.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Bye-bye.

chapters.summary: Morano describes being asked to sign an NDA before visiting Borden and says council attorneys called it a patient confidentiality form; Dalton explains DHS policy PB 2026-001, state social services law 136, and NYC identifying information law, saying it protects resident privacy but not building conditions.
chapters.title: Morano questions Dalton on shelter NDA policy and confidentiality law

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Just to follow up on what Councilmember Paldino and Councilmember Wan alluded to, since they both brought it up and it was on my list as well, the issue of the so-called NDAs.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Before I visited Borden Avenue, you know,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: DSS had sent me a document, which they referred to as an NDA, saying I had to sign it to go.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And obviously, I was not going to sign an NDA because I want to be able to share broadly exactly what I observed, good, bad, ugly.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I forwarded this to the attorneys for the city council, and they said their view was that it was not an NDA, that it was a patient confidentiality form that just

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: prevented me from sharing any confidential patient information that I got.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Then when I got to Borden Avenue, one of your staffers for DSS, who was very professional and terrific, he asked several of us that were visiting, oh, did everybody sign their NDA, which added to a little bit of the confusion.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm wondering, since several of my colleagues have brought this up now, what exactly is the policy with respect to signing a form before you visit Borden Avenue or other shelters?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And what does that form actually prevent someone visiting from sharing?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you for the question and the opportunity to clarify there.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: All right, so DHS, I mean, I'll just start with, of course, we have

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: a requirement, us and our providers, to keep our clients, whether veterans or other people experiencing homelessness, their safety and confidentiality at the forefront of our work.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: This is where people are living and staying, and they have a right to privacy in those settings.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so we have codified the way we grant access to our shelters in a DHS policy and procedure.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It's got a name.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It's DHS PB 2026-001.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We can make that available to you.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It's a long document and has different specifications for different types of visitors because you can imagine there are different types of visitors.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And there is a section on elected officials.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Part of the reason we codified this and require signing the agreement that you referenced and others have referenced is it's the way we comply with, again, state and local law, right?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So there's the state social services law 136 and New York City administrative code 23-1201 through 23-1205, the identifying information law.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So we, both the form and the way we proceduralize that in our document are the ways that we comply with, again, state and federal, state and local.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: local law.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: To be clear, this is about protecting people.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: This is not about talking about a tarp.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: People are free to talk about the tarps that they saw with their own eyes, about the food that they saw or that they heard about.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Anything else except for people's

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: people's identity and their privacy, right?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So that's the piece that we are trying to protect and are required to protect under state and local law.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so if there, you know, perhaps it is an area where the administration and council need to have more discussion, but we have

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: documented that protocol in a whole procedure and are following it in accordance with the state and local law.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Now, I don't think any of my colleagues, even a rule breaker like Councilmember Wong here, would ever reveal confidential patient information to anybody.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So just to be clear, before any of us are able to visit Borden Avenue, we do have to sign this document.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Is that a requirement?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It is a requirement.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I have a number of other questions.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Councilmember Wilson.

chapters.summary: Wilson acknowledges the difficult job, cites a Gothamist report on high outreach spending and poor results, and asks how to improve coordination among outreach workers and agencies.
chapters.title: Carl Wilson questions Dalton on street outreach coordination

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Hello, Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I want to turn back to street homelessness and outreach.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: The other honorable chair brought up.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: You know, I know you have a very difficult job.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And, you know, when we have these conversations,

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Passions run high, but I would like to acknowledge how difficult of a task that you have.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And I know from interactions on issues in my district, I appreciate how hands-on you've been personally coming to walkthroughs, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: So there was a report in Gothamist that highlighted the exorbitant amounts of money that are being spent on outreach, yet the results seem to be going in the other direction, in a negative direction.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: What yet it compares to under the Bloomberg administration when there was outreach that was individualized for each borough that a decrease had happened, a 40 percent decrease in street homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Yet now I'm hearing from meetings that I'm having in district.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: One of the problems is about the amount of outreach workers.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Not being able to coordinate, not being able to share information, leading to individuals on the street having like four, five different agencies approach them, ask them for shelter, but there's not a coordination or like individual strategy.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Who's the front, you know, who's leading that?

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: So how do we, how do we fix that?

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: How do we get the coordination together so that these people doing this really difficult work

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: are getting a result.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Thank you so much for the question and for raising the issue that I agree is a very important component of the way we engage and serve our unhoused neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And this, too, is an area that I'm taking close look at.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We've been holding meetings across city government and with state partners as well, looking at those very issues, and we'll be very pleased to share more in the homelessness plan.

chapters.summary: Wilson asks if results focus on engagements rather than placements; Dalton says placements are tracked for contracted outreach and acknowledges the need for more accountability.
chapters.title: Wilson asks Dalton how outreach engagements are measured

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And how are the engagements measured?

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Because that was another criticism in the article, that the results that we're looking at are more about times engaged and not necessarily the outcome, the placement.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: So how do we retool that so that we're really focusing on the outcome we want, which is placement?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, to my understanding, we are tracking placements for the contracted outreach that we support.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But I understand the broader point of accountability and wanting to ensure that those efforts, not just the funding, but the efforts of people are leading to the results that we want to see.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And again, think we can do more as a city and as a set of partners to serve that group.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And it starts with that outreach.

chapters.summary: Wilson asks why 311 street homelessness reports moved from NYPD to DHS; Dalton says DHS can better determine encampments and use the data to target outreach strategically.
chapters.title: Wilson questions Dalton on 311 encampment routing change

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And there was also, I believe in September, there was a bit of a, and something I'm getting a lot of questions about in the community.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: a change in terms of when there is street homelessness reported.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: The 311s for that are no longer routing to NYPD, going to DSS.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Could you help us understand the reason for that change and what the broader policy goal is by...

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Changing who's responding first to the engagement?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I think it is, it's a small, but I think important change to have the right people going to the event, right?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so what you're talking about is that 311 calls to identify whether a reported encampment is a homeless encampment moved from the NYPD to DHS Homeless Services.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So now we're the people who go out there and not only determine whether it in fact meets the legal definition of an encampment, but can do outreach and engagement.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Also, having that data entirely within our domain allows us to use it to, again, sort of target outreach to the places where it's needed most, where people are calling about encampments,

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: even if it's not a legally defined, it's not an encampment under a legal definition, it's a signal of concern in the community.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So now we can use that information to deploy our outreach in more strategic ways.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So I'm pleased that we were able to, we are able to do that work now and not only

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: identify and make the legal determination of whether it's an encampment or not, but put to start outreach if we hadn't already been working with those folks already.

chapters.summary: Wilson asks who does initial assessments after 311 calls; Dalton says it could be contracted outreach or DHS employees, agrees different skills and clinicians are needed, and notes work with the state SOS team.
chapters.title: Wilson asks Dalton about multidisciplinary outreach teams

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And my some colleagues at the state level have introduced legislation that would require for multidisciplinary teams to go out to do this engagement.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Would how so that just who is going to do those initial assessments on?

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: When the 311 is placed, is that a DSS worker?

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Is that a contracted outreach?

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Who's the first point of contact?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It could either be a contracted outreach or a DHS employee.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And you didn't quite ask, but I do agree, if that's where you're headed, that different skills are required at different parts of an engagement and a core theory of engagement is also required.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Peers can be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: People who have experienced unsheltered homelessness or homelessness can be excellent at talking with folks.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And there are times when clinicians are required.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We do have clinicians on our team at DHS, and our contracted providers also have clinicians on those teams.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And we work closely with the state's SOS team as well.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Of course, we need that kind of multidisciplinary approach to handle various types of encounters.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And, you know, I just want to say, too, that I do.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I welcome a perspective from Pittsburgh.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I welcome a new way of looking at this because I think the agencies get.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: We kind of get bunker mentality.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: This is the way we do things, and this is how it's done.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: And so I respect that you've been on the job for six months, but I'm hopeful that we can have that outside perspective really peel back all these layers here because it's resulting in folks not really getting connected to what they need.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: So thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Councilmember Wong.

chapters.summary: Wong says he visited Borden with Julie Won, was told they needed DSS and mayor's office permission, entered anyway, and was told not to enter bathrooms or the library; he says problems were exposed because they did not sign NDAs.
chapters.title: Phil Wong describes being denied entry at Borden Avenue

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: By sitting in the Veterans Committee, members here have a charter-mandated duty for oversight.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And with that in my mind, that's why I visited the Borden Avenue shelter with Councilmember Julie Wan a couple weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And with us were members of American Legions and members of VFWs and the press.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And they heard, and this was documented, that the person in the front desk told us that we cannot go in unless there's permission.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: From the Department of Social Services and from the mayor's office.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And despite that, Councilmember Julie Wan and I decided to go in anyway.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And then there were several people following us, telling me, I'm going to quote, Councilmembers, you're not allowed to walk down that way.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Council members, you are not allowed to enter that bathroom.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Council member, you are not allowed to enter that bathroom.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: allowed to open that door, that library door.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Those were the replies I got, and a lot of it was in video.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And what I wanted to say is it wasn't accommodating at all.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And certainly your office did not give the approval for Council Member Julie Wan and I to visit the place because we didn't make an appointment, we didn't sign an NDA and so forth.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And I can say for certainty,

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: We are talking about the problems right now because we did not sign any NDAs.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: That's how these problems get exposed.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Those roof leaks did not start a couple months ago.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: They've been leaking for years.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Veterans did not have enough food for years.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: No one is talking about it because the people who visited had to sign NDAs.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So I want to, okay, we're here to get answers.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And that's why I serve here.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Otherwise, I have other committees to serve.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I care about the homeless shelters.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I care about the veterans.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And I serve in CAP meetings, the Pan Am, Pan Am shelter.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It's the end of my block.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I've been to their CAP meetings.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I know how it works.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: These issues have been talked about again and again in CAP meetings.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And nothing got discussed openly.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Nothing got brought up until this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Now.

chapters.summary: Wong says tarps and buckets at Borden are unacceptable, says the flood wall implies long-standing flooding, criticizes DHS and the mayor's office as unaccommodating, and says a roof should not take three years.
chapters.title: Wong criticizes DHS handling of leaks and flood wall

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay, I want to correct something.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It says, DHS is managing leaks in the sleeping area with tops.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: This statement alone is very, very disappointing and heartbreaking because it sounds like that's how DHS is handling all the leaks in all the shelters with tops.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And I want to add to that, it's not just tops of the buckets too.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Buckets right underneath the top collecting the water.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And then after the rain, when the water flows somewhere else, they have to move the buckets.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: That's what's happening at Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And when you say that in the testimony, it sounds like that's how you're handling leaks in other shelters.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And this is very, very unacceptable and very, very disgusting.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And then,

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: A new flood wall will be built behind the building.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So by telling me that, you're saying there's been a flooding condition in the Borden Avenue shelter for many, many years, and nothing is being addressed until now.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And again,

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Chairman Morano said it correctly.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It doesn't take three years to finish a roof.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And I want to be on the record that DHS and the mayor's office have not been accommodating at all.

chapters.summary: Wong says the kitchen is subleased to a culinary school and veterans told they cannot participate; Dalton says spots are reserved and veterans can participate and will look into it; Morano then gives Wong extra time for his birthday and calls on Hudson.
chapters.title: Wong questions Dalton on kitchen sublease and culinary school access

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: My question is this.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Let's start with the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: The kitchen is now being subleased to a culinary cooking school.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Instead of being a facility that's available for veterans to cook their food, to heat up their foods or do their own cooking.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: This is happening right under our eyes.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And it's my understanding that whole site should be a shelter.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Why is it part of it is being leased to a culinary school?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I testify to this, right?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We see that same commercial kitchen and think it could be a better use to the people that are staying there.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so we are pursuing changes and looking at the opportunities that that kitchen could provide.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I heard concerns about the food.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I see the opportunity with the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We see the provider, ICL, also sees that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And those things take a little bit of time.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But we are looking at the food.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I will say I don't think it's a problem to sublease parts of the kitchen to other training programs.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: There are spots reserved for ICL residents.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: These are programs.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: These are workforce programs that give people a skill.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so I think there's not a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: But veterans cannot sign up to the culinary school.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: That's what they told me.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: In fact, there are spots saved.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It is a long program.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: My understanding is it's a six-month program.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It takes place during weekdays.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And a lot of the veterans who are staying at Borden Area Shelter are also working another job.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So they may not apply and may not take advantage of that.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But it is not correct that they cannot participate.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Well, at least two veterans, when I stood outside with Council Member Juan, told me that they want...

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: to sign up for the culinary school and they were told that they have to go somewhere else to learn how to cook, not in that school.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: All right, which is truly shameful because you let this happen, that that facility is meant for veterans and you let this space to be subleased to a culinary program and the veterans living in there have no access to it.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: All right, and that's unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And you're saying that's not happening.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: That is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I will look into it further.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But I've asked these questions already and been given assured answers that that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I should also just point out that...

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I mean, your point is still correct that we agree that that kitchen is underused for the people staying there.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But the program is run by another one of our providers and serves a similar population, a non-veteran population.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: But it does serve people.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yeah, but isn't it common sense that if those facilities, the veterans shelter, then the kitchen should be available at all times?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: To the veterans?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I agree and testify that that is something that we want to take a look at.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay, my next question.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We'll come back to you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We'll come back to you, and we'll give you a little extra time because I understand it's your birthday.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Happy birthday.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: May all your wishes come true.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Keep in mind, give them gentle answers back.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Chair Hudson.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Hudson says she has visited the shelter twice, criticizes colleagues for conflating city, state, and federal roles, says no shelter allows residents to cook their own food, and commends the administration's investment.
chapters.title: Hudson addresses colleagues' comments and clarifies kitchen policy

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I just wanted to take an opportunity to address some of the things that I've heard from my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: because I've been to the shelter now twice in the last week or so, and I've seen some of these things with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: First, I want to say, I know Councilmember Palladino mentioned an embarrassment of sorts.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I think for me, what's most embarrassing is when my colleagues in the city council cannot

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: make a distinction between our roles and responsibilities, the roles and responsibilities of the mayoral administration and those of the federal government and state government.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And so we have a federal government that, first of all, I want to say I commend the administration for the investment that you have made in upkeeping the shelter.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Despite the challenges that have been presented, I would say, by the federal government, a federal government that doesn't believe women should be serving in the military, that doesn't support

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: certainly many more than just women, members of the LGBT community, so forth.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I think there's just, there's been a conflation of certain statements.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And to be clear about the kitchen specifically, there is no shelter provider that allows residents to cook their own food.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: In any shelter.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: That is not something that is allowable regardless of who is staying in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: So to imply that a kitchen should allow

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: residents to cook their own food is just inaccurate.

chapters.summary: Hudson says ICL will testify later, hopes grandstanding members stay, acknowledges disappointing conditions, says the system does not work for the most vulnerable, and commits to continued oversight.
chapters.title: Hudson calls for systemic fixes and dignity for veterans

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Secondly, and I know that members from ICL who runs the shelter will testify later on, and I hope that everyone who is here

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: to grandstand will stay for all of those testimonies and then ask some more pointed questions.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: You know, it's my understanding that there is a service or an opportunity for people to use the kitchen and that the program specifically has a lot of requirements that not every resident is willing to participate in.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And so I look forward to hearing some of the nuances of this.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And this is not to say that there aren't disappointing.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Circumstances at the shelter.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: It's also not to say that we shouldn't be treating our veterans with far more dignity and respect.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I saw a gentleman last night who had a carton of juice that my three-year-old should be drinking, not a grown man.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And so these are systemic issues that I know, Commissioner Dalton, you are invested in addressing.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And I know the folks who are running not just this shelter, but every shelter across the city are also invested in addressing.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: We have a system that doesn't work for the most vulnerable people who rely on it the most.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And those are the things that I hope to be able to get to the center of, not just at this hearing, but at every other hearing that I will be chairing

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: as chair of the General Welfare Committee with oversight over the Department of Social Services, including the Department of Homeless Services.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: So much of our system does not work for those who need it.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: But I just wanted to make sure that on the record, I had an opportunity to clarify some of the points because it is disappointing.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: when folks use opportunities like this to leverage really vulnerable people and vulnerable moments and really hard work that people do every single day to make light of

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: the realities that are happening.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And also, when so much of it is happening from a federal government that some of the people support and then want to complain about the city government not doing what is actually the job of the federal government.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: So I just wanted to state that for the record.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Morano says he disagrees with some characterizations of the federal government, notes five public panels, says federal, city, and state could all do more, and stresses there is no disagreement on ending veteran homelessness.
chapters.title: Morano responds to Hudson and emphasizes shared goal

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'll just add, you know,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I think it's no secret that I disagree with several of the characterizations made of the current federal government administration.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We have five panels of the public that are here to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And what I want to do in this hearing today is get answers from the public, from both of the commissioners that are good enough to be here, and help that testimony inform what we're doing on a legislative basis.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And the truth is, could the federal government be doing more for veterans?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So could the city.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So could the state.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So could we all.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I really do believe that all of my colleagues here, Democrat, Republican, whatever, are all approaching this hearing and this issue from a place of passion and wanting to do better for our

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: veterans.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I love that I'm in a body where we can have such spirited disagreements about those sort of things, but there's no disagreement that there should be no veteran homelessness.

chapters.summary: Morano asks how many of the 209 placed veterans are still housed; Donnie Smalls says all 209 are still housed and none returned to shelter, and Morano requests retention rates at 6, 12, and 24 months.
chapters.title: Morano asks Mata and Smalls about housing retention

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: With that, before we get to Councilmember Wan, I see Commissioner Mata is getting very antsy because no one has asked her a question in a while, so I'm not going to do that to you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Your testimony says that 209 veterans were placed into permanent housing in fiscal year 2026, and that 702 veterans answered an aftercare call, and those are encouraging numbers.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But how many of the 209 veterans are still housed today, and do we know how many have returned to homelessness?

utterances.speaker: Yesenia Mata
utterances.text: Thank you for that question.

utterances.speaker: Yesenia Mata
utterances.text: I will pass it on to our Associate Commissioner, Donnie Smalls, who handles the aftercare component.

utterances.speaker: Donnie Smalls
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Donnie Smalls
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: Donnie Smalls
utterances.text: Co-Chair.

utterances.speaker: Donnie Smalls
utterances.text: Donnie Smalls, Associate Commissioner for the New York City Department of Veteran Services, also a combat veteran.

utterances.speaker: Donnie Smalls
utterances.text: Currently, all 209 veterans are still housed.

utterances.speaker: Donnie Smalls
utterances.text: None have returned back to shelter.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So the housing retention rate.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: At six months, 12 months, 24 months.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Do we know what that is?

utterances.speaker: Donnie Smalls
utterances.text: I can get those numbers back to you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I think the committee would value that as well.

chapters.summary: Morano asks if visits are atypical, cites a flyer warning residents to clean urine containers, and asks if he can visit unannounced; Dalton says current policy requires notifying DSS, and the coordinated visit with Hudson was unannounced to the provider.
chapters.title: Morano questions Dalton on unannounced visit policy

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Let me also follow up on one of the issues.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: that several of my colleagues raised, which is this issue of was our visit there atypical, right?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: A lot of us remember Hogan's Heroes when the Geneva Convention would come to town.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: The POW camp was a very different place than on a typical day.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There was a flyer distributed, which was shown on the news and elsewhere, essentially warning folks to clean up containers of urine and things like that.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: When I visited, ICL told me that, one, it's not atypical to have these sorts of flyers to encourage people to clean up their space.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And they also said that they would welcome unannounced visits from me or any of my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There seemed to be a little confusion about what the policy in terms of unannounced visits is.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: What exactly is the policy when it comes to unannounced visits?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Am I able to go to Borden Avenue today, tomorrow, next week without telling anybody?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: As long as I sign that form that you referenced earlier.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I will start and I'll see if the Deputy Commissioner has anything to add there.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So as I mentioned before, and you probably don't want me to go through the whole thing again,

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: we have a policy and a set of procedures for entrance into our shelter system that are our way of complying with both state and local laws.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: As DHS and the deputy commissioner can speak to that and a number of other people can make unannounced visits to check in on the conditions as part of our oversight responsibility.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And I think you would count this as an unannounced visit.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Last night, Chair Hudson and I

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We coordinated, right?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So she coordinated with our office.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: She signed the appropriate agreement.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And without telling the provider, which is the important part, and I can assure you I did not tell the provider that we were coming, we showed up at Borden Avenue Shelter around 8 p.m.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Last night.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And so that is an unannounced.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So I don't want to belabor the point because, but we do have a very cynical public, as you know, especially New Yorkers, right?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And it's a cynical public that I'm sure already thinks I'm being way too nice to you guys.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But a lot of folks will say that if you're telling the DSS commissioner,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Hey, you know, we're coming to this shelter today.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: That's not exactly the same as just a regular unannounced visit of me going without telling you.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yeah, so that is not currently in our allowed procedure.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And again, which is routed in state and local law.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: There are some circumstances and, you know, it's written in those procedures, like the Coalition for the Homeless under court order.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We've protocolized ways that they can...

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Do visits of that kind.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And it is, I think, possible to get to that kind of an understanding, but it is not our current approach.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We must follow the current and DHS, and certainly our providers must follow the current procedure that is laid out and allows us to comply with the current state and local laws.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Councilmember Wan.

chapters.summary: Won asks for the difference between state and local laws and DHS policy, asks staff to read the law on record, and Dalton says the law is lengthy and can be cited, clarifying the NDA is about resident privacy, not building conditions.
chapters.title: Won asks Dalton to read state and local laws on shelter access

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Morano and Chair Hudson.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Can you expand?

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Because I would like to know the difference between which state and local laws you're referring to and what is HPD, sorry, DHS policy.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So, right.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So there's a DHS policy and it and we can share this policy.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It's called DHS PB 2020, 2026, 001.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: So we can we can provide that to council.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And it is one of the ways that we are requiring with state social services law 136.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Could you read the laws?

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So that the public can hear, because there seems to be a lot of different opinions on what is law and what is policy internally.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: I would have to look up that law in order to read it to you here.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Is there someone on the staff who could make sure that before this testimony time ends that we can have this publicly read on record?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: What I'm hearing is it is a pretty lengthy law, and we could cite that for you so everyone can read it on their own.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And can you help me understand what is the necessary paperwork that was signed by Chair Hudson?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: It is the nondisclosure agreement that we ask anyone to sign, that we ask certain visitors, and that's most visitors, to sign who are visiting the site.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So if we sign an NDA agreement, how are we supposed to talk publicly about the atrocities that we see inside?

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: No, thank you again for allowing me to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: The NDA and the laws are strictly about the people who stay there.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: They are not about tarps or food or any building conditions you might see.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: If you see what you view to be showers that are not respecting people's privacy, if you see a ramp that you do not think is ADA accessible, if you see food that you don't think is ADA accessible,

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: is edible or at the quality we should be providing, you can absolutely report that.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: We just, of course, have to protect the people who are staying there.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: And that is the entire purpose behind the DHS protocol as well as those laws.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Okay, so when we come for a visit and we have signed an NDA, as long as we don't disclose the individuals who are currently residents of the shelter, we can speak publicly about the atrocities that we have witnessed during our oversight visit.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Won asks why veterans are punished for the federal disagreement; Dalton says the city is covering the full cost of the shelter, DHS is responsible, and expenses will be reported in the future financial plan.
chapters.title: Won questions Dalton on $4M funding differential

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And then the next question that I had was for the $4 million.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Differenced like the delta that is going to now be $1 million in funding.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And I want to echo the sentiment that Chair Hudson has said that we want to respect trans service veterans as well as women who serve.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And we support that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: But I want to understand why it is that the veterans themselves are the ones being punished for this disagreement.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yes, thank you again for the opportunity to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Nobody is being punished for this.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: The city is covering the full cost of the shelter.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So for the $4 million differential.

utterances.speaker: Erin Dalton
utterances.text: Yes, the city is covering the full cost of the shelter.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Okay, so the $4 million that we're no longer getting from the federal government will now be part of the city's budget.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And would that be coming from...
