utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Coco Culhane
utterances.text: Really qualified to say and would hope that it's really the veterans going through the system that we're listening to.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Miller introduces Homeless Services United, says the DHS NDA policy hinders volunteers, interns, donations, and events, and says no other city agency has this requirement.
chapters.title: Kristen Miller testifies on DHS access policy and NDA burdens

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: I'm Kristen Miller, and I'm Executive Director of Homeless Services United.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: We are a coalition representing 55 nonprofit organizations who provide homeless services across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: I want to thank both Chairs Murano and Hudson for this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: I think it's a very important hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: very important topic, as do our members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: And I also very much appreciate your comments in support of the nonprofits who do this work every day to ensure that people experiencing homelessness have the best experience they can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: I think the issues raised today are rooted in a couple of things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: One is about partnership between nonprofit providers that are contracted to do this work on behalf of the City of New York and that partnership with the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: I think the first issue that we've been talking a lot about is the New York City DHS access policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: It is the legal, moral, and ethical duty of New York City shelter providers to provide the safety, security, and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: privacy of the people they serve and the staff that they employ through established security measures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Regardless of the procedures that DHS has put out, it is their duty to do that, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: And while the vast majority of people coming into shelters have very good intentions, sometimes people don't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: And it is the obligation of the shelter providers to make sure that everybody comes into their building has the best intentions, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: So they all have screening processes for ensuring that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: So we have to create a policy that is welcoming, a balance of welcoming of the community and also protecting the people who are inside the building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: But our members are reporting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: that the DHS protocol is a hindrance rather than a help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: This is because DHS must sign off on all NDAs before individuals can enter shelters, and the process is then unnecessarily burdensome.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: To our knowledge, no other city agency

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: has this requirement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: This is unique to DHS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: And the result is that organizations, volunteers, and others who are eager and willing to contribute to shelters face additional barriers to giving their time and resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Some very specific examples that we've heard from our members are that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: National organizations have been contributing volunteer supplies like diapers and books,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: shelter makeover opportunities, have decided to offer their donations of time and resources to other places like New Jersey, Philly, Westchester County, where they don't have these same onerous requirements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Are still able to protect the people inside the buildings'safety and privacy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Providers have been prohibited from sister organizations coming on site for health fairs, job fairs, service fairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Delays and assignments to other city-funded programs for social work interns because the NDAs must go through the university's legal departments, which was taking longer than six months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: So social work interns, we're so understaffed, we rely on interns all the time, and now we're having a hard time getting permission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: for them to do their placement at shelters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Back-to-school events were canceled in August.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Donations of diapers, hygiene kits, books were not able to be brought in by the volunteer groups and philanthropy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: And these shelter kind of spruce-up days have been canceled as these national corporate offices couldn't get to reviewing the NDAs in time.

chapters.summary: Miller says nonprofits face aging facilities and pending new need requests totaling nearly $1 billion, supports Intro 897, but warns against unfunded mandates on nonprofits.
chapters.title: Miller describes funding delays and supports Intro 897 with caution

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: The second issue that we've been talking about is funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: These buildings that have been mentioned are in aging facilities that were not originally intended.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Nonprofits get annual budgets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: They include maintenance costs, but not for...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Leaky roofs, broken pipes, the inflation of food, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: So they have to go to DHS to get more money in the budget.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: That has to be improved by OMB.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Then it has to get into the individual nonprofit's line item budget in order to get paid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: This takes a long, long time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: DHS has about 1,900 pending new need requests going back to 2018, totaling, at our estimate, nearly a billion dollars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Some requests, as we've heard, go back years and years, back and forth, and yet the work doesn't get done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: The increases don't get into their budgets that they need to run their programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: I think overall, we need to focus on the people and not the processes, and we have to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: make sure that the funding gets to the right place at the right time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: I just want to note that we are in support of Intro 897.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Of course, we want adequate planning ahead of severe weather events, but there's one note of caution, and then I'll finish, is that we are concerned that this will be an unfunded mandate of more work on the nonprofits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: They already operate under hundreds of policies and procedures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: So please, whatever you do, take into consideration that it doesn't put an onerous burden on the nonprofit, but that government and nonprofits are working in partnership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Miller
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Derek.

chapters.summary: Coy introduces himself as an Iraq War veteran and NY Health Foundation officer, says veteran homelessness is rising again, cites high suicide rates among homeless veterans, and recommends embedding suicide prevention and improving data.
chapters.title: Derek Coy testifies on veteran homelessness and suicide prevention

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Hudson, Chair Murano, and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: My name is Derek Coy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: I'm a senior program officer at the New York Health Foundation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: I'm also a former sergeant at the United States Marine Corps and veteran of the Iraq War.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: It's been unfortunate to hear about the funding loss and issues and shelter conditions for veterans in New York City that are experiencing homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: But it is encouraging to see so many folks on the council and government, the nonprofit sector, and various advocates coming together to address these concerns because it is clearly needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: After declining nearly 90% between 2011 and 2022 and reaching historically low numbers, veteran homelessness in New York City is rising again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: As recently as 2024, the numbers had surged nearly 30%, threatening more than a decade of progress and underscoring the need for renewed investment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: But like most issues veterans face, homelessness is not the sole concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: Veterans in New York City already face rates of suicide approximately 45% higher than our civilian counterparts, but we know these rates aren't evenly dispersed throughout the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: A recent study from VA and Yale researchers offers one of the most comprehensive examinations to date of the link between cumulative social disadvantage and suicide risk among U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: Veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: And the patterns were alarming.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: Veterans in the top 5% of social disadvantage were more than 20 times as likely to report suicidal thoughts or behaviors than those experiencing the least hardship.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: The associations were even stronger among veterans with a history of mental health conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: VA's most recent national report on veteran suicide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: It underscores this as well, pointing out that the suicide rate for those with either a diagnosis of homelessness or who have received homeless program services in 2024 was 72 per 100,000,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: meaning the suicide rate among veterans experiencing homelessness was 118% higher than among those with housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: Furthermore, patterns of veteran homelessness also differ by gender.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: Women are the fastest growing demographic in the veteran community, and at the same time, documented cases of homelessness were greater for female veterans who died by suicide compared to male veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: These findings reinforce the importance of addressing the social and economic drivers of veteran suicide, and we strongly recommend that efforts to address veteran homelessness also prioritize suicide prevention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: Through expanding and embedding suicide prevention across mental health and social service programs, ensuring all unhoused veterans are screened for suicide risk and referred to appropriate services,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: exploring options for expanding peer mentorship for mental health, and improving data collection to identify veterans at greater risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: That last point I'd like to harp on because when we're talking about veteran homelessness, the way we define veteran is how we count them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: And according to VA, depending on the character of your discharge, if you were kicked out because of your gender, identity, sexual orientation, or systemic racism, you might not be counted as a veteran.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: And again, when we look at suicide rates for veterans, these are those fortunate enough to have access to VA health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: So these numbers are very likely an undercount and not looking at the severity of the situation for those most vulnerable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: We commend the committee's effort to meet the needs of veterans experiencing homelessness and share your commitment to New York City's veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Coy
utterances.text: I hope you will look to myself and the New York Health Foundation as a partner and resource for this work, and thank you again for the opportunity to testify this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Coy.

chapters.summary: Morano calls Michael Matos, Mike Matthews, Anthony Bird, Sharon White, Mike Munoz, and Angel Sansa.
chapters.title: Morano calls next public panel

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We will call up our next panel.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Michael Matos, Mike Matthews, Anthony Bird, Sharon White, Mike Munoz, and Angel Sansa.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Why don't we begin with Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Matos, and then we'll work that way.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Just turn your mic on and keep it close.

chapters.summary: Matos says Five Borough Veterans filed records requests, describes Borden conditions, council members being denied entry, a DVS satellite office on site, and asks why the city walked away from funding.
chapters.title: Michael Matos testifies on Borden conditions and oversight failures

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair Murano, Chair Hudson, and members of both committees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: My name is Michael Matos, and I serve as the president of the Five Borough Veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: On September 24th, we learned from the press the city of New York had withdrawn from the VA's grant and per diem program, a $4 million a year funding source that has supported the Board and Avenue Veterans residents for 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: With residents'futures uncertain and both governments blaming each other, we filed records requests with the VA and the Department of Homeless Services on the same day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: The VA has since responded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: The city quoted us a date of December 30th.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: What followed exposed failures at every level of the system responsible for these residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: On October 24th, excuse me,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: On October 1st, we went to Borden for an investigative interview with the press to hear from residents about how the funding dispute would affect them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: What they told us about conditions inside raised serious concerns, and those concerns reached the city council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: That day, council members Julie Wan and Phil Wong arrived to use their oversight authority under the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: City Charter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: The administration told them they needed an escort and a scheduled appointment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: I stood beside Councilmember Wan as she was verbally berated on speakerphone by the mayor's office for using that authority.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Residents report abuse, inevitable food, cramped quarters, broken facilities, and a roof that leaks where they sleep and a kitchen they are not allowed to use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Some have gone a week without an edible meal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: At this time, we are in conversation with the Department of Investigation to investigate the shelter's operator, the Institute for Community Living, and with the city comptroller to audit its contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: If the operator falls short, the community is calling for a new provider from within the veteran community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: We are also concerned about how the Department of Social Services handles oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Before a visit, the department asks elected officials to sign a form.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: It treats as a nondisclosure agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Chair Murano shared that form with us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: It is a patient confidentiality agreement, not a nondisclosure agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Protecting residents'privacy is important, but using that form to limit what access elected officials can have at a facility does not protect residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: We have also seen firsthand what advance notice makes possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: On October 5th, residents contacted us because they were being pressured to rush a cleanup before the Commissioner of Social Services arrived that evening, a visit that was never announced to the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: We went to board in that night with Council Members Wong and Wan and confronted the Commissioner directly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: That is our central concern with how oversight visits are handled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: When the city knows who is coming, problems get covered up instead of fixed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: The site only works when officials see a facility the way the residents live in it every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: We also recently learned that the Department of Veterans Services has a satellite office inside the board and building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: City staff whose job is to serve veterans have been working under the same roof as these conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: On October 7th, I asked Commissioner Mata directly whether her agency knew.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: She did not answer the question and spoke only about her agency's role in benefits and services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: The commissioner is now our community's last voice in city government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: When veterans ask what she knows and what she's done about it, they deserve a direct answer, not to avoid the question as the well-being of these residents hang in the balance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Finally, the funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: For nearly 20 years, the VA's grant and per diem program has helped pay for this shelter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: The city has said it's walked away because the new grant terms would have barred transgender veterans from receiving services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: No veteran should be turned away, and we support that principle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: But we reviewed the VA's records release with the offices of several elected officials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Unless that language sits on a redacted page, there is no such requirement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: We asked the administration to explain why I walked away from this funding, how much city money will replace it, where that money will come from, and how it will get

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: guarantee that no veteran on boarding goes without services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Every level of this system owes our veterans accountability and transparency, the operator, the agencies that oversee it, and City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Our community is told often that it is valued and honored.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: We hear thank you for your service at every parade and every ceremony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Borden Avenue shows how little priority our veterans actually receive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: We ask as council to hold each level accountable, so those words mean something to the veterans living at boarding today and across New York City going forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Matos
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Munoz says the VA offered $1.3 million and the city turned it down, cites a bed decline from 154 to 8, and demands canceling the ICL contract, resignations of Dalton and Mata, a comptroller audit, and space for VSOs at Borden.
chapters.title: Mike Munoz demands accountability and lists five demands

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chairs and members of the committees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: My name is Mike Munoz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: I'm a post 9-11 global war on terrorism veteran and the current veterans caucus chairman of the New York Young Republican Club and a longtime advocate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: I'm not here to ask politely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: I'm here to demand accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: The VA offered this city $1.3 million for homeless veterans at Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: This administration turned down every dollar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Now the taxpayers are covering a bill Washington offered to pay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: The VA's own award list show that grant and premium beds tied to New York City fell from 154 veteran beds in fiscal year 2024 to just eight fiscal beds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: 8 in fiscal year 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: There's a 94.8% decline in listed capacity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: New York State now ranks 21st in the nation in total awarded beds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: A drop like this raises serious concerns about whether homeless veterans in this city can get transitional housing at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: The award lists alone do not tell us whether beds actually closed or whether other programs replaced them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: That is exactly why this council needs answers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: On October 1st, two members of this council went to inspect that shelter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: They were kept outside for hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Inside, they found leaks and tarps hanging near the cots where veterans sleep.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Then the mayor's office demanded nondisclosure agreements before council members could tour, and residents say they were ordered to clean the building

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: before the commissioner's visit, a visit the residents were told about and this council was not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: This is not a funding dispute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: This is a failure of leadership, and failure has names.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: In the military, leaders lead from the front.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: When leadership fails, they are relieved of their command.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Here are our demands in five points.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: One, cancel the contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: The Institute for Community Living was paid to run Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: It failed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Not one more dollar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Two, Commissioner Erin Dalton must resign.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Her agency oversees this shelter, walked away from this funding, and left this council standing at the door.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Three, Commissioner Yesenia Mata must resign.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: I respect her service in uniform, but her own department has an office inside that building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: On October 7th, she was asked whether her department knew about these conditions, and she could not give a straight answer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: When veterans of Borden Avenue needed a fighter, they had a commissioner down the hall who could not say what she knew.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: The full audit by the city comptroller of every dollar paid to run Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: and every dollar now spent to replace the funding, this city refused.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: And five, open the doors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: The Department of Veteran Services cannot be the only way a veteran gets help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: The Department of Veterans Affairs itself gives veteran service organizations space in its own buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Give the American Legion, the VFW, the DAV, and every organization willing to serve these veterans space inside Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: To this council, you have subpoena power, budget power, and oversight power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Use all three.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Get the documents now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Do not let this end with a hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Veterans hold the line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: We held it overseas, and we're holding it here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: We will be back until these men have what they earned.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Munoz
utterances.text: Matthews.

chapters.summary: Matthews asks how the VA measured performance to reduce the grant, questions whether the refusal was based on redacted terms, notes VA policy on transgender care, and asks if ICL staff are veterans or trained in military culture.
chapters.title: Mike Matthews questions VA performance and transgender policy

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Mike Matthews.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I'm the co-lead of the Staten Island Service Member and Veterans Task Force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: And I have to say that, you know, the percentage of those who've served is increasingly small, and I personally believe that we really need to bridge the gap between the civilian and the military population.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: However, I'm only going to really address a couple of issues having to do with the funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: As I understand and how it's been explained, the original contract with the VA was for $4 million.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: standing was the renewal amount was reduced to 1.35 based on performance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I would like to understand how or whether performance was measured by the VA to result in such a dramatic decrease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: Question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: Also, in terms of the other issue,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: of the $1.3 million grant not being accepted because it did not, again, I've heard that it did not allow providing service to transgender veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: The Freedom of Information document received from Five Borough Veterans did not reflect

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: However, there were sections redacted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I would also like to understand whether the refusal of the grant was because of a redacted portion of the grant, which would be interesting to look at,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: whether it could have resulted from a misreading of the grant's intention or some other explanation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I did a little research on this, and the VA News reported that back in April of 2025,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: effective immediately, VA will not offer sex hormone therapy to veterans who have a current diagnosis or history of or exhibit symptoms consistent with gender dysphoria.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: Unless such veterans are already receiving care from VA, such veterans

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: Veterans are receiving such care from the military as part of their eligible veterans diagnosed with gender dysphoria.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: They will continue, eligible veterans will continue to receive comprehensive VA health care, which includes preventive and mental health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: So the question I'm saying is,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: It doesn't seem like the VA policy seems to be to continue to treat and assist transgender veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: However, the Freedom of Information had redacted information which didn't include that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I don't know what the answer is, but I'm just saying it's a question I think that needs to be addressed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I just also want to mention one thing about ICL.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I know they're not here, but I have a question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: We know veterans trust veterans, and I wonder if any of the staff on ICL are veterans, and or if not, are the civilian employees?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: Provided with military culture training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Matthews
utterances.text: I think I will leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Matthews.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Sir.

chapters.summary: Byrd says he is a former Borden resident, conditions need improvement, suggests a new building, says DVS staff helped him find housing but his landlord will not renew his lease, and describes kitchen and food restrictions.
chapters.title: Anthony Byrd describes Borden conditions and lease termination

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: How are you doing, sir?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Just bring that mic close to you so we don't miss a word.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: My name is Anthony Bird.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I'm a former veteran.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I'm a former resident of Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Okay, I apologize for my attire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I didn't know it was going to be formal today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: You look great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I like the sweatshirt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Yeah, you can't, you got to beat common sense into people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: But I've been to Born to Napping twice, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Fortunately, I met some great people through there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Yeah, conditions in Board Avenue need improvement, without a doubt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I would say, personally, get them a new building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Simple as that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Get them a new building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I had these people behind me right here help me find housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Smalls, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Ward over here, Sam and Maya, they helped me find housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: You know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: And unfortunately, the landlord doesn't want to renew my lease, so I might have to go back to Borden.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: There's no telling just yet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: But Borden needs improvement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Like they say in the shower area, in the cafeteria area, in the food area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I just left there last December.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I've been in my apartment in Long Island City not even a year, and they've sent me a 90-day notice of termination not to renew my lease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: So, yeah, Board and Avenue needs help with them showers, with the food.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: In my opinion, if you don't like a job, you shouldn't have it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: If you like your job, you'll excel at it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Me personally, when I got into the Army, unfortunately, I had KP quite a few times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: For who don't know what KP is, it's a punishment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: And they used to send me to the kitchen all the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: That started my cooking career.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I've been cooking ever since.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I don't like nothing else but being in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: You want to do construction?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Call him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: You want to do auto repair?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Call him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I'm just saying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I'm just saying as an example.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I like kitchens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: But no, you can't cook at Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: And as of last year, I don't know how the policies have changed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: But last year, no, you couldn't bring food into Borden Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: They had a little room to the side that you had to eat it in, or you could bring potato chips and cookies in because they had the vending machines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: They sold it anyway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: So yeah, you could bring snacks in there, but you couldn't bring cooked food really.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: You had to sit in the side room and eat it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: As far as Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Wong was talking about with the culinary arts program, last year you couldn't get in because I asked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Like I said, I'm a cook.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: I asked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: And no, you couldn't get in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Policies may have changed between then and now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: We'll see.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: But as far as that's concerned, you have good issues, you have bad issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: There's some that can be addressed, and there's some that can't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: You know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: Like this gentleman said, we all need to get together and put our heads to it and see if we can't work it out together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Byrd
utterances.text: That's all I have to say.

chapters.summary: Morano says the city should help before homelessness, offers his contact information, and asks about culinary program eligibility; Byrd says he was told residents could not participate.
chapters.title: Morano offers Byrd help and asks about culinary program

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Bird.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I appreciate really hearing your perspective.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano

chapters.summary: Brown introduces herself as a Cold War Navy veteran and community board chair, supports Res 0560 to allow VA home loans for co-ops, describes H.R. 1803 and its 3.25% fee, and recommends a city initiative.
chapters.title: Dr. Cleopatra Brown testifies in support of Res 0560

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Just want to begin by saying thank you to the chair, Morano, to the co-chair, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Hudson, and the New York City Council Committee on the Veterans, Committee of Veterans, the Council Committee of Veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: My name is Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Cleopatra Brown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: I'm a Cold War Navy veteran and a homeowner in the Brownsville section of Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: I served from August 1982 to May 1988 and also reservists in the New York City Navy for two years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: I'm also the chairperson of Brooklyn Community Board 16 Veterans Affairs Committee, and I serve on the Joint Community Boards 3, 8, and 16 Veterans Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: On behalf of the Joint Veterans Committee, we are in support of the Resolution 0560-2026.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: The United States Department of Veterans Affairs VA Home Loan Guarantee Program has been a cornerstone for veterans for over 80 years and is one of the most essential benefits earned by eligible veterans,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: active duty service members, and qualifying surviving spouses, providing pathways to sustainable home ownership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: and long-term financial stability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: The VA Home Loan Guarantee Program currently supports the purchase of eligible single-family homes and condominiums, but strictly exclude veterans from using their benefits to purchase co-ops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: This limitation creates a significant barrier for veterans in New York City and other high-cost urban housing markets, where co-op apartments make up a substantial share of the available home ownership market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Veterans who have earned the VA home loan benefit through military service should not be prevented from fully utilizing that benefit simply because an affordable

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: home ownership opportunity is structured as a cooperative rather than a condominium or traditional single-family residence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: In 2006, Congress recognized this issue and authorized a temporary five-year pilot program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Unfortunately, administrative delays caused it to underperform.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: The VA took nearly three years to publish the lender guidelines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Furthermore, the agency failed to market the benefit, leaving most eligible service members unaware of the option.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: The pilot program expired unrenewed in 2011.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: The Fair Access to Co-ops for Veterans Act of 2025, H.R.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: 1803, was introduced in Congress to amend Title 30.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: of the United States Code and improve the Department of Veterans Affairs Loan Guarantee Program by providing permanent authority for VA guaranteed financing for the purpose of residential co-ops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Federal guidelines currently allow veterans to use their VA loan benefits to purchase single-family homes, condominiums, townhomes, or manufactured homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: However, H.R.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: 1803 will add a 3.25% loan fee for co-op housing loans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: The New York City Council should examine this proposed 3.25% co-op loan fee and consider whether it will create an affordability barrier for veterans seeking to purchase

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: co-op apartments, especially given significant monthly maintenance charges and co-op board financial requirements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: While H.R.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: 1803 requires federal legislative action, New York City Council Resolution

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: 0560-2026 has an important opportunity to help develop an effective implementation framework for VA-guaranteed co-op housing loans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Expanding VA-guaranteed finance cooperative housing will allow veterans to have equitable access to the home ownership benefit they earn through their military service,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: provide veterans with greater housing choice, increase access to home ownership,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: allow veterans and their families to build equity and generational wealth, and help address disparities in veteran home ownership in high-cost urban communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: On behalf of the Joint Veterans Affairs Committee, we recommend that the New York City Council establish a coordinated initiative involving the New York City Department of Veterans Services, DVS, the New York State of Housing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Preservation and Development,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: New York City Housing Development Corporation, the New York City Department of Consumer and Workers Protection, participating financial institutions, co-op housing, and veteran-serving organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: This initiative should establish veterans co-op home ownership counseling, financial workshops, education on the VA loan eligibility, down payment or closing cost assistance and referrals to participant lenders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Identify cooperative housing opportunity in New York City that may qualify for VA guaranteed finance under future federal requirements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Examine co-op corporation policies concerning down payments, financial reserves, debt-to-income ratios, board approvals, and transfer restrictions to determine how these requirements can interact with VA lending

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: standards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Coordinate home ownership counseling, financial readiness workshop, and information about applicable down payment or closing cost assistance programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: And engage banks, credit unions, and other lending institutions to identify financial and regulatory barriers affecting the VA Guarantee Co-op loans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: To promote transparency and accountability, I recommend that the New York City Council commit on veterans, establish guardrails for collected information on participant lenders,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: eligible cooperative developments, veterans application, loan approvals and denials, and complete purchases in accordance with applicable privacy requirements.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And Dr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Brown, I'm just going to ask you to wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Just to wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: In addition, request a formal interagency comprehensive report from DVS, HPD, HDC

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: to identify any additional steps that may be contingent on congressional actions and that they may require additional city resources or legal authority.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Cleopatra Brown
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and consideration.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Graham.

chapters.summary: Graham introduces himself as VAB chair and VFW legislative leader, supports Intro 1051 and Resos 560 and 634, describes the property tax exemption history, says GPD funding must remain, questions the ICL contract, and suggests severing it.
chapters.title: Ryan Graham testifies on Intro 1051 and Borden contract

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Funny, I have good morning on here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chairs and members of the Committees on Veterans and General Welfare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: My name is Ryan Graham.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I'm a U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Air Force and Iraq War veteran.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I serve as the chair of the New York City Veterans Advisory Board, a member of the VFW's National Legislative Committee, and state legislative vice chair for the Department of New York VFW.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: My testimony draws on these responsibilities and my continued work with and support of the veterans of the foreign wars of Department of New York legislative leadership team.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I strongly support Introduction 1051 and Resos 560 and 634.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Together, these measures address keeping veterans in their homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Expanding access to home ownership, and strengthening the organizations that help veterans navigate life after service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Introduction 1051 deserves particular attention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: In 2018, I was the original writer of this property tax exemption proposal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Advanced through the Queens County Council VFW Legislative Committee, and then on to, which was introduced by State Senator Joe Adabo and Assemblywoman Stacey Pfeffer-Romato.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: That work helped establish the foundation for my continued advocacy on this issue, which I have carried forward through my ongoing role with and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: support of our Department of New York VFW legislative leadership team.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: For me, this is a commitment that began eight years ago and continues today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I thank Councilmember Frank Marano, Chair, and the bill's co-sponsors for advancing this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I'll pause for a second.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: A lot of, I've noticed quite a few legislatures are jumping on board with this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Buffalo just did it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: And hopefully it doesn't take eight years to do this here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Hopefully we get this through right away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Furthermore, for these veterans, the financial consequences of service can last a lifetime.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: A permanent disability can limit employment, increase the cost of daily living, and place additional responsibilities on family caregivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Property taxes remain a recurring obligation even when a veteran's ability to earn additional income is permanently constrained.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: This exemption would provide meaningful stability and help eligible veterans remain in the communities they call home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Housing policy must also include

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: preventing displacement before a veteran reaches a shelter door, keeping an eligible disabled veteran in an existing home preserves family stability, community connections, and access to care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: The council now has an opportunity to turn state authorization into tangible local relief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I urge prompt

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: passage accompanied by a clear implementation plan from the Department of Finance and Department of Veteran Services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: The same commitment to housing stability must guide our response to ongoing issues at Borden Avenue's residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: As chair of the New York City Veterans Advisory Board, I take these concerns seriously.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: We will be providing recommendations to the mayor and the city council in our 2026 New York City VAB report on the way forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Those recommendations will follow further review.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: The points I offer today reflect an initial assessment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: First, funding through the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Department of Veterans Affairs GPD program must remain available to support veterans who need those services, these services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: GPD supports transitional housing and services that help veterans move toward permanent housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I'm going to move forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: At the time, preserving federal support requires a serious examination of who is entrusted to deliver the services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: There is a legitimate question about whether the current provider should continue to hold the operating contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: That question should be answered through a document, a review of contract compliance, conditions, staffing, resident concerns, corrective actions, and permanent housing outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: The city's operating contract and the VA's GPD program must be examined by the responsible authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: With coordination between them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I'm going to stop right there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: I got more here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: My take, it's going to come out from the VAB that something like this, there's way too much evidence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: One of the biggest smoking guns was a FOIA request that I saw.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: In a year and a half period, three, on average three a day, 911 calls.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: That's a problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Somebody here in one of the prior panels mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Honestly, I mean, something like this, if it's been going on for a long time, you know, it's, it's, and then the other big concern, I happen to be there and well, in the background with Councilman Wong, Councilwoman Julie Wong,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: New York City Council, you're the oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: You should have access to these facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: But like I said, we're going to have something extensive in our VAB report, especially on housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: So the council and the mayor's side will see it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: But, I mean, from an initial assessment, I mean, I've been around the block a long time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: Something like this, honestly, I'd sever the contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Graham
utterances.text: And I would just do a complete reset.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Graham.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: First of all, thank you for all of the work that you've done to lay the groundwork for Intro 1051 and the property tax exemption for disabled veterans that we're trying to pass.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as far as your comment about oversight, the differences of opinions that you've heard from council members

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: today, I think the one thing that unites all of us is that we all agree that part of our oversight responsibility should be able to include dropping.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: into Borden Avenue and similar shelters whenever we'd like.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Figueroa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa
utterances.text: Shame on you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa
utterances.text: We are all created equal regardless of race, religion, color, gender, etc.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa
utterances.text: And we all deserve respect and we demand respect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa
utterances.text: I'm not going to bring that up right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa
utterances.text: And that's that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa
utterances.text: That's that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa

chapters.summary: Meggett says being allowed to speak is not being heard, compares asylum seeker spending to the DVS budget, asks where the urgency is for veterans, and says DVS staff are not the target but elected officials must prioritize veterans.
chapters.title: Herbert Meggett criticizes budget priorities for veterans

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: On behalf of Veteran Action Now, I'd like to thank this committee for the opportunity to speak for some of New York City's most vulnerable and often forgotten residents, our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: But let me be clear, being allowed to speak is not the same as being heard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: And being thanked for our service is not the same as being served.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: According to the New York City Comptroller, New York City recorded approximately 1.47 billion in asylum seekers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Spending in fiscal year 2023, $3.75 billion in 2024, and $3.2 billion in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: These expenditures supported the city's emergency response, including shelter and services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: By comparison, the city's preliminary fiscal year 2026 budget proposed $5.9 million for the Department of Veteran and Services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Approximately $494,000 less than fiscal year 2025 adopted budget.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: To be precise, that was a preliminary proposal, not the final fiscal, not the final adopted figure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: There are differences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: There are different spending categories for the Department of Veterans Service budget.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Does not represent every dollar the city spends on veterans, but that distinction does not erase the question for us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Where's the same urgency when a veteran needs a place to live?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: This is not an argument against helping asylum seekers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: It's not an argument against asking veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: This is an argument to asking veterans not to accept neglect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We should not have to compete with other vulnerable population for basic dignity and safe, affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: When veteran homelessness is not simply a housing problem, it's a statement about our priorities, budgets, reveal what government is prepared to fund, policies reveal what government is prepared to protect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: And when veterans remain homeless or cannot afford to stay in the city that they call home, speeches about gratitude are not enough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: To the mayor and the members of this committee, if you believe veterans are a priority, show us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Show us the funding, the housing commitments, the enforceable protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: And the measurable results do not point to a proclamation when we are asking for a place to live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: I also would like to make an important distinction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Department of Veterans Services is not the target of my criticism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Its staff

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: must work within the resources and policy framework that this administration and the city council provide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: On several occasions, I have contacted the department on behalf of veterans in need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Its staff responded promptly and helped resolve those issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: For that, I offer them a sincere thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: But I intend to keep the needle on the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Put responsibility where it belongs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: With the elected officials who set the priority, write the budget, and decide what gets done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: In my experience, this city, this state,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: And this administration has not demonstrated the commitment veterans deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: About a year ago, I personally asked the mayor whether he was anti-veteran.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: said to me no and asked why would I ask that question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: I told him I had not heard him mention veterans during his campaign for mayor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: That absence mattered to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: So did his decision to endorse someone for Congress, whom I believe had an attack and belittled our community when veterans are disparaged.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We deserve leadership willing to stand with us, not political endorsements that leave us questioning where do we stand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We serve to defend the Constitution of the United States.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We should not return home only to feel invisible by government we serve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We are not asking for special treatment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We are demanding that the city promises mean something.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We are not war criminals, and a cardboard box is not a medal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: A shelter bed is not a housing policy, and warehousing veterans is not the same as bringing them home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We are your neighbors, workers, parents, caregivers, community leaders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: We deserve safe, stable housing that's genuinely affordable, not merely labeled affordable while it's beyond our reach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: So do not simply thank us for our service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Show us in your budget and your policies that our lives matter after this service ends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Herbert Meggett
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Magid.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Just point the microphone towards you and keep it close.

chapters.summary: Kelly introduces himself as a young Marine veteran, shares his mother's death and COVID funeral, describes his work as a veteran outreach specialist, and mentions harm reduction and an RFA contract for veterans.
