utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Also, you naming your place of employment I don't think is a negative.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And certainly, I mean, they can't hold that against you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Unless you're not in sick today and you're here instead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: So, you know, this is actually one of the first times I've ever been able to do like, okay, like this is veteran focused.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: That's literally in my job description, veteran outreach specialist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: So I feel like I was supposed to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: I will say I probably could have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: Practice the words a little bit better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: I'm a little nervous now, but yeah, like hopefully I answered your question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: Did I?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: If not, please tell me because I'm learning so much today, so much.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Yeah, and like Chair Marano said, you're doing a great job.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I'm just trying to get a better understanding as far as the work that you do and your experience.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: When you're doing your outreach, how are you specifically identifying who is a veteran that's sleeping on the street?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: You talk to him.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay, so if somebody is not a veteran...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: Then they would still be able to receive harm reduction services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: So if they need like a wound care kit...

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: So you're talking to everybody and then you're giving particular focus to those who may be veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Kelly
utterances.text: And I'm giving referrals to everyone else.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Terrific job.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Then let's go to Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Gibson.

chapters.summary: Gibson says he is a current Borden resident, has been there since February 2025, describes personal challenges, says Borden needs help but there is nuance, and discusses library access, food rules, and staff accountability.
chapters.title: William Gibson describes life at Borden with nuance

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Good afternoon, all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: My name is William Gibson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Last place I served was the Fighting 69th Unit, not too far from here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: What you would call, they would say, they would call me the NBC, the NBC guy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I'm the chemical operations specialist for the Army.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I would like to say that beauty is subjective and there's nuance to everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And I say that because I currently stay at boarding and I've been there for a little while.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I had to go through numerous personal challenges while being there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I've been to nine funerals since I've been in boarding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Family, friends, and also one of those was including my father who died last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I would like to say that.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I would like to say that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Yes, boarding does need help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: There's improvements that should be made.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: The building needs to be fixing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You know, the food needs help, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: But there's nuance to everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: The library, you know, we have access to the library, but when there's a group going on being that that's the public place, then it's closed off for that group to commence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: After the group is over, then the library is open back to the public, but it's also closed overnight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because the rec room in the cafeteria open for everybody to hang out at overnight and watch TV and talk and do things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: There's nuance to everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: There's good soldiers and bad soldiers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: To the rules of eating, we're not allowed to bring food in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And if you do, there's the blue room that's off to the side, which is a small little space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You can eat there, but you can't go no further than there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Once again, there's nuance to everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: With the staff being there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: It's a two-way street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You have to meet with the staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: They put out notices, appointment slips.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: There's even, you know, slips that come out and say, hey, when they're going to do a room check.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So there's an accountability there that's also on the residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Keep your place clean.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Keep everything dressed right, as we would say in the military.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: But that ain't the case with a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And this is not to put everybody on front street, but accountability can go both ways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You know, the staff can't chase us all down and have us meet with them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Now, me, when I first got there, I was very silent because you don't know how to speak to anybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: About your situation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: But while being there, I've had time to self-examine me, my life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And now I have a team that's working with me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And when I need to talk, they let me know that I can talk, which I'm still trying to get used to accepting that because I'm used to doing everything on my own.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: But I would say y'all as the political chair that you vet all your information wisely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You check out the place and vet it wisely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You listen to the complaints wisely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You watch what ICO do wisely because that's your job, the vet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And you should be checking out everything, just not a little small pocket of things saying that's that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: No, check out everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Try to get a good look at the place when it's running during its regular operation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Then you'll get to see the full picture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You know, so there's good and bad at boarding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Good and bad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And yet there's a lot of things that needs to be fixed and worked on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And when it comes to staff, yeah, they're not perfect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: But at the same time, you know, we have to do our part as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So it's a two-way street inside.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And I just hope that, you know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You have to learn to listen to understand, not listen to respond.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because listening is truly a skill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Also, watching and seeing what's going on.

chapters.summary: Morano asks the biggest problem; Gibson says GPD funding allowed extra family time, staff have been understanding, urine containers help disabled residents, and maintenance cleans regularly.
chapters.title: Morano asks Gibson about biggest problems at Borden

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And so, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Gibson, just to be clear and for everybody, you're currently a resident at Gordon?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: How long have you been there?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I've been there since February of 2025 with a break in between to bury my dad and came back.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: What is, if you had to pick, the single biggest problem with conditions at Borden right now?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Wow.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Or if you want to pick two, pick two.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: See, that's wild.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because now you're saying pick one thing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Well, pick two.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Well, it would be great to have the GPD come back because that allowed extra time for me to be able to reach out with my family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because I have two grandchildren currently in the ACS system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And with the GPD rule, they was able to see me longer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because now they can know that they have a family member that will see them every so often and they're not alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Once the GPD rule got cut.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: What's been your experience in terms of how helpful the ICL staff has been in terms of getting you to transition into more permanent housing?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Well, with the staff, they've been very understanding of me as a person.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because what you got to understand is that all the residents there at boarding got an issue going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Now, whether or not they're going to, you know, look at it or they're able to talk about it, not talk about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: See, that's another issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because what I feel the staff has done with me, they tried to understand me first as an individual.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So when I first got.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I wasn't able to really talk and express myself like I do now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And they allowed me the room to sort of come to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And once they heard everything that I have going on, they were like, oh, wow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: You know, so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: They do their best, I feel, not to breathe down your neck, but at the same time, meet with them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So the thing that if you go there and bring up my name, watch how the staff reacts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because even when I was silent, when that notice came under the door, I made sure they saw me so that their work can be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because you got to remember, they get audited.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: My last question, and then I'll defer to colleagues, is we heard a lot from people and in the press that maybe the picture that I got when I visited Warden Avenue wasn't an accurate one.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Maybe they tried to get everything cleaned up and give residents warnings, hey, clean up your urine containers, so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Based on your experience, is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Do they try to put their best foot forward when there are visitors?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Or did I get an accurate picture of what happened when I visited?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Well, I can speak to that very well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So with that being said, the maintenance staff there cleans the place very regularly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All the time, irrespective of who's coming.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: All the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: I will say it's been more cleaner of late because we've had, from my understanding, that the amount of people that's been there were very low at one point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: But now within the past couple of weeks, new face, new face, new face.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Within the past couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So with that being said, when it comes to urine containers, I would like to say that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Get on the residents to keep their rooms clean.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Because you have a personal space where other people and other residents, other shelters don't have a personal space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Keep it clean.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And when it comes to the urine containers, dump them, wash them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Contain them so when the staff needs to come in your room and do a room check, they don't have to be exposed to that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And you should be, and let's also be clear here that, okay, look, there's a lot of guys in there that got disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: If it wasn't for those urine containers, we would be moonwalking on urine every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: From their rooms to the bathrooms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And there's two sets of bathrooms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: There's one in the cafeteria.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And there's the main bathroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So those gerund containers are a help to those guys.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Just keep them clean.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Anybody else have questions for Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Gibson?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Figueroa
utterances.text: Chair Hudson and then...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: There's nuance to everything.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: There absolutely is, and I appreciate your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I just wanted to verify, and maybe I'll have to get this from somebody else, but the GPD rule, do you know if that was related to the federal funding?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: From my understanding, I was told that, you know, that now...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: The facility now is ran totally by DHS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: And with the GPD rule being gone, the extra time I was allowed to be out, I can't do that no more.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And extra time you're allowed to be out, meaning out of the shelter?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Councilman Wong.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you, Jeff.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Do you have access to the library's computers and books right now?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Yes, just not overnight.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Do you have internet?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Yeah, there's internet, dude.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: There's internet that you can visit websites, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: Yes, and we can also sign in on our phones, but there's a 24-hour lockout rule.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So meaning that, you know, I'm a techie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So, you know, when you're logging into the site,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: and onto the, to get access, it shuts you down after 24 hours and you have to re-log in again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: That's not a bad thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So that way, whoever's running, you know, the site administrator, they can do their cleanup and you have to log back in again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Gibson
utterances.text: So that's the only, that's the only rule with that.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you, Jeff.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Appreciate it very much.

chapters.summary: Morano calls Joe Bellow and other names not yet heard and invites them to testify.
chapters.title: Morano calls Joe Bellow and other remaining speakers

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I had called up Joe Bellow earlier, but I don't think he was in the room and heard me call him up.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Bellow, I'd love for you to come up and be heard.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Also, I'm going to just call up a few other folks whose names I called but may have left the room or may not have heard me.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So if any of these people are in the room, they can come up as well.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Timothy Terrain, Angel Sansa, Sharon White, Philip Ventachingue, and Carmelo Stewart.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If any of those folks are here, come on up.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Be seated at the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And you're going to learn how it's done from a professional, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Bellow.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Bella, whenever you're ready.

chapters.summary: Bellow asks why the VA reduced funding and why the city rejected the reduced award without more discussion, says veterans and the LGBTQ community are being pitted against each other, supports Intros 1051 and Reso 560, and disagrees with Reso 0634's timing.
chapters.title: Joe Bellow questions VA funding reduction and city rejection

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I apologize for not hearing my name called.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I appreciate the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I'll be real quick.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: There was a lot said today, and I'm still kind of processing some of the things I've heard, some of the things that were said.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So you all have my testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: One of the things, though, I think still goes back to what I had initially been writing about when we were talking about Borden was, you know, why did the VA reduce the funding for Borden?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: And I appreciate you, Council Member, for trying to reach out to the VA and get that answer, even if we're probably not going to get it, but I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: And then the second question, which I didn't hear quite a bit, I would have liked to have heard more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: or of was why did the city reject the reduce award without the conversation about the transgender veterans?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Because I think the problem is, is for me, it personally, I felt like we were being pitted against the LBGD community and we're the same community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So I would have liked to have

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: heard something a little more about why that money wasn't taken, especially if you're looking at 231 beds and there's only 168 residents, you still had the space to do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So I think that was the two kind of questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: In terms of what's happening inside of Borden, I think...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: The last gentleman who spoke, I think he was very...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Transparent about what he's seeing, what he's witnessing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I've kind of heard and seen the same thing as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I don't think that, again, there is a reason and rhyme to everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I think I know that if I was inviting you over to my house, I would be cleaning up my house prior to you coming to visit me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So I think that some of it is common sense as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I just think there was too much going on in terms of whether the council members should have been able to go in unannounced, which I think they should have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: And I think that I appreciate Council Member Hudson for bringing up the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: About what it says that they can come in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I just think that there needs to be a better policy around that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: that and making sure that it does protect the privacy of the veterans themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: The other thing I guess I'll talk about has been the roof.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: That has been a very big concern to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I mean, going back as far as 2022, Councilmember Bob Holden has been bringing that up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: And it was asked again in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: And I've kind of heard the same answer now going back four years now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So at some point, you know, the rubber meets the road.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: We have to figure out, like, when is this roof going to get done?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: You know, look, I recognize that the building is old.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Personally, I would like to see it demolished and then, you know, maybe rebuilt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Maybe find somebody that would want to rebuild it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: And build it not just maybe as an SRO, but put some workforce development in it, a real kitchen, a bigger library, things like that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So I think that's been one of the other problems for the roof that's bothered me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I would also like for the council to obtain a timeline from DHS identifying any work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Not just the roof, but any work within Borden that's being done, whether it's, you know, what's outstanding, what's expected to be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: In terms of...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: DVS at the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: At the Veterans Summit, I know the Commissioner talked about revamping the housing unit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I'd like to hear more details about that, or at least have you explore more details about that and how that is going to affect not just veterans outside of Borden, but veterans within Borden as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I also think that we need to go back, the council needs to go back and take a look at the December 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Controller's report about the housing unit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I think that there needs to be some, just a review.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: What has changed from that report?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I mean, it's almost been a year now, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: We're in October.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So what's changed?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: What's better?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: It's being revamped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So how does that make things better?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So I think those are clearly things that we can do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Just to wrap up, because again, there was a lot to take in from this hearing, and I'm going to have to rewatch it like probably two or three times just to get all the data from it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I support intros 1051 and reso 560.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I disagree with RESO 0634 in its current form.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: That's your Veteran Organizational Awareness Week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: As you know, the Skindy Council passed a resolution a couple of years ago with Councilman Dinowitz that made November Veterans Month.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: My feeling on that, Rezo, is that...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: the week would get lost because it is Veterans Week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So I would like for you to consider maybe redoing that resolution to make it either the week prior or the week after.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: I think you might have a better...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Better peace with that, especially since, you know, what do we do to promote VSO week, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: So that's it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joe Bellow
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Bellow.

chapters.summary: Morano asks if anyone else wants to testify, reminds the public about written testimony, and calls Leroy Becton.
chapters.title: Morano invites remaining in-person testimony and calls Becton

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Before we turn over to the Zoom testimony, I want to make sure that everybody who would like to testify in person has gotten an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If there's anybody who is here to testify in person that hasn't done so, raise your hand and the Sergeant at Arms will get a card to you and make sure that they can testify.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We'll get these folks.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Set up.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as we get these folks in the queue and get them ready, I'll remind everybody that's watching this either online or on cable that if you didn't know about this hearing in advance,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: but you want to contribute something in terms of the oversight topic or any of the legislation we're considering today, you absolutely can submit testimony in writing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I've been getting some emails of folks that weren't able to be here or had to leave, and they submitted testimony in writing, you could just email testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: That's council.testimony, excuse me, testimony at council.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: nyc.gov and that testimony will be taken into account and the record just as much as everybody else's.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And, you know, I didn't get a chance to mention intro 1051 earlier, but I appreciate Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Bellow and Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Graham referencing it in their testimony.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Just for clarity's sake, for people that aren't up on this, the governor and the state legislature, they passed a bill.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Creating a property tax exemption for anyone that's listed as 100% disabled, service-connected, that's a veteran, as certified by the VA.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And basically that legislation would exempt those folks from paying property taxes.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But the trick is the municipalities or the counties in the state have to opt in.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So as of now, even though the state legislature passed that bill and the governor signed it, that changes.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Nothing for any veteran in New York City unless we, the city council, act.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So my hope is that this will be a great way to allow veterans who are disabled to be able to stay in New York and afford to stay in New York and not have to move elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I'm really hopeful that we'll be able to pass that in time for Veterans Day.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And so far, the response that I've gotten from many of my colleagues has been very favorable.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I had called.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Leroy Belton earlier, but I would love for him to come up.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: He's a former ICL client, or it might be, excuse me, Leroy Becton, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Come on up and be seated at the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And is there anybody else in the room here that wants to testify in person?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right, we'll get your card in as well.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Becton, right?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Becton.

chapters.summary: Becton introduces himself as a disabled veteran and artist, describes homelessness after service, thanks the council for follow-up, and says taxpayer dollars and accountability are at issue.
chapters.title: James Edward Becton III testifies on accountability and follow-up

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Last time I met you were in the spring.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's great to see you again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Indeed, my good brother.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: And all of you, I give you gratitude and thanks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: I am James Edward Becton III.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Becton, if you will.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: I'm an artist, a disabled veteran, once of the Army, department head at Chemical Corps as well,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: entrepreneur, founding executive artistic director of the Becton International Black Theater and Arts Consortium, sitting here right now as a proactive citizen,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: and in tandem as a proactive advocate with Fibro veterans and all the other veterans to give note and gratitude to you all who have taken the time to make time to bring this issue to the light of day at this time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: After having served to protect this nation's ideology, which has been under assault for reasons quite antithetical to the very contract and constitution that I,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: we, did in fact both vocalize, sign, and exercise, some of us too, expiration,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: I experienced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: homelessness, not once but twice after coming out of the service, and at no aid or assistance did I get from the VA because a part of that was VA issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: I am an artist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Both of these times I was enveloped and nurtured by my community of artists, and had it not been for that said community, I could have very well been a tenant in this here facility that we are investigating right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: We are all here today because of care, accountability, and taxpayer dollars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: The care, a transitive verb, is because we are concerned enough to be here, as we all are, to make this note.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Accountability, or in this instance, one of many, a severe lacking of accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Our taxpayer dollars, the very ducats we've been mandatorily relinquishing since our first W-2s, the very cash that is taxed upon receipt,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: taxed to spend, taxed to save, taxed to pass down, taxpayer dollars that are functioning everywhere in our faces, but here at our home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: In our own backyard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: This is on a micro level, an exhibition of what's happening on a quite macro level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: This is an issue regarding the lacking and fulfillment of a contractual obligation to properly remunerate with care the very citizens and service members, veterans of these United States.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Upon my introduction to Representative Wong, his immediate rebuttal to me was, I work for you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: And that is exactly the correct answer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: And as we all sit here today vocalizing and testimonializing why this is important, I'm here to give you all gratitude again for taking up the reins.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: We, as service members, look to you as elected-led service members to do the right thing for we the people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: And we're making our voices of support for these actions taken here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: So I thank you kindly, truly, for your time and attention, for being proactive in dealing with these issues that don't only just deal with veterans, but everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: But today it's about veterans, and I give you grace for paying attention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: And this is what I said to you when I met you last time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Good, sir.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: The only thing I requested of you was follow-up and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: And the fact that we are here today, these many months later, means exactly that, that you are exactly following through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: And I give you all grace and gratitude for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Becton.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I do hope when Councilmember Wong told you that, you at least wished him a happy birthday.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Oh, well, I'm wishing you a happy birthday now, brother, because you're doing the do, and that's exactly the representation that we're needing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Edward Becton III
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Becton.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right, I believe we have one final gentleman in person, and I'll apologize in advance if I mispronounce your name, but it's Rana Bissassar.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Please correct me.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right, great.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Have a seat and begin whenever you're ready, and then we'll move over to the Zoom testimony.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You can turn the mic on, keep it close to you.

chapters.summary: Bissassar introduces himself as a retired Master Sergeant and Bronze Star recipient, a peer counselor at Borden since April 2024, and describes the aftercare program and community meetings.
chapters.title: Rana Bissassar describes peer counseling at Borden

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: My name is Rana Bissessor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: and I'm a retired Master Sergeant of the United States Army.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: And a Bronze Star recipient for action in combat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: I graduate from the University of Maryland College Park Overseas Campus, where I got my bachelor's in Bachelor of Science in Business and Management.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: I have continued my education since, earning my New York City Certified Peer Specialist credential in 2024.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: And certified recovery peer advocate in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: My testimony today to tell you is a story of my transition from training and leading soldier during the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: leading soldiers in war during the first half of my life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: To support people experiencing homelessness during the second.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: I'm a peer counselor at Borden Avenue Veteran Residence since April 2024.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: I draw on lived life experience and professional training

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: to offer non-clinical emotional

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: support, guidance, and mentorship.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Peer counseling connects in real who had overcome adversities such as mental health,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: challenges, substance use disorder, trauma, or academic barriers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: With other familiar circumstances.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: My Bronze Star and my certified recovery peer advocate

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: and my New York City peer special certification reflect two complementary foundations of my work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Military experience that helped me build trust with the veterans and peer support training that equips me to support residents in their recovery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Having counseled hundreds of soldiers on career progression and personal conduct, I bring mentorship-centered approach to peer support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: I strive to model the resilience

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: needed to navigate life's darkest moments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Demonstrating how a soldier discipline and a counselor's empathy can work hand in hand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Also recognition from Governor Scott in Florida, who also underscore administrative experience, bring to my work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Extending my commitment to service from the field, the office, and the boardroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: I completed my peer counseling internship with Borden and have brought his approach and commitment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: to excellence to my work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: We're from day one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: I appreciate the opportunity to share how compassionate and dedication guide me, my support for board and clients today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: One of my main job also I do is the aftercare program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: And I talk to veterans on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: Once a month at Borden, we do the community meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: All the staff will introduce themselves and tell them what they do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rana Bissassar
utterances.text: And I tell them plainly, I'm here to help you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you for your service.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And a real honor to be joined by someone who's a Bronze Star recipient.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thanks for what you've done for the country as well.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Nelson introduces herself as a Gold Star spouse and VAB vice chair, says veterans describe showers like jail, calls for an independent review, veteran input, and a Tunnel to Towers location in NYC.
chapters.title: Dr. Mecca Nelson testifies on dignity and conditions at Borden

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Well, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Hi there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: It's a pleasure to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I just have a few things to say, and I would like to call this,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Testimony, dignity after service, and safe place to call home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair and Co-Chair Hudson and distinguished members of the New York City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Thank you for holding this oversight hearing on veterans homelessness in New York City and for the opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: First off, I do want to say

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Thank you to Phil and Julie for being a disruptor of change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: For doing what needed to be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: That created this space right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And when I heard about what was happening, it hurt my heart dearly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: My name is Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Mecca Nelson, and I serve as vice chair for the New York City Veteran Advisory Board.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I'm also an ambassador for the Institute for Veterans and Military Families and an ambassador for the Tunnels to Towers Foundation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And I am also a small business owner and an executive director of nonprofit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Above all, I stand before you as a U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Army Gold Star spouse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: My late husband, United States Army Sergeant Mario Nelson, was killed in combat in October.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: First, 06, I became a widow at the age of 24, raising our three-year-old daughter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This month marks 20 years since his sacrifice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: That loss continues to shape my commitment to those who serve and the families who serve alongside them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: bring that personal experience to my work and in the community to this testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: When I speak about our veterans'dignity, safety, and well-being,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Do you know I speak from...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Heart that understands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Today I ask us to listen closely to our veterans and respond with care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: It deeply concerns me to hear veterans describe the showers in their shelter as a resemblance of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: being in a jail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: We must listen to how those conditions make them feel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: They are telling us that the place where they live does not feel like home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: It does not offer the comfort of sense of safety they need to rest and begin to heal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This affects their mental health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: They come out with one situation or one issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And as they go in and they're in this world and being inside that shelter, they come out with other things behind it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And deeply concerns me to take this space and to even be here right now speaking about this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: These are individuals who served our country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: They deserve to be treated with respect, compassion, and care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Their needs should be attended to, their concerns should be heard, and their living conditions should support their health and well-being.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Our veterans deserve clean showers with privacy, safe surroundings, and a welcoming place to rest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: No veteran should have to plead for these basic necessities or feel forgotten while seeking help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: A shelter may be temporary, but dignity, warmth, and care offered within it should be considered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: We cannot ask someone to rebuild their life while overlooking the conditions in which they are expected to heal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: How can you heal living in those conditions?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Trauma is a serious thing and trauma can affect you mentally, emotionally, spiritually, and physically.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: They served our country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: We have a responsibility to care for them with dignity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I respectfully urge the council to ensure a thorough, through independent review

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: of the concerns raised about the facility, including its structural conditions, sanitation, accessibility,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: and sustainability for the residential shelter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: If it cannot provide safe, healthy, dignified conditions, the city must provide an appropriate alternative and a supported transition for every veteran affected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I also ask for a clear process

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: through which veterans can report concerns about fear of not being taken care of right, receiving timely responses, and participate in decisions about their care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: How can you make decisions for the veterans and not have them in the room to say yay or nay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: How would you know what they really need if you're not asking them?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Nelson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Wait, I'm not done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I have more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I have more to say.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If you could bring it to a close.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Yeah, I will.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I do feel that that building, and I agree with Joe, that building should be demolished.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And I do have, I do, with my suggestion that I feel, I know that Tundra Towers is a foundation that is building villages, veteran villages across every state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: However, we don't have one out here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Tunnel to Towers have over 20 veterans nationwide, but we don't have a location in New York for our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And this is what I have to say so that I don't fall off anything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: My recommendation is that New York City should provide or have or give Tunnel to Towers a location in New York

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: so that they can have their own independency to do what they do because they're doing the work that they're doing without any issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Help secure space to reduce unnecessary obstacles that allow tunnel towers to operate independently to carry out their mission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: New York City has an opportunity to do more for our veterans and support our organizations working to help them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Our veterans deserve a place that feels like home, a place of comfort, belonging, and hope.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Members of the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: The decision made in the room become someone else's daily reality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: They determine where a veteran sleeps tonight, whether the veteran can shower with dignity, and whether they feel heard, respected, and hopefully...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And hopeful about tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Let our appreciation become action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Let our oversight lead to meaningful improvements and let every veteran who turns to this city for help know your service

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: matters, your voice matters, your life matters, and you deserve a safe place to call home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Nelson.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Next, we have Christopher Leon Johnson.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Johnson, you can begin as soon as you're unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I want to make this clear that this ministry, I think the city council needs to start fighting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: No, it's a lot that y'all guys can't do because with the come to veterans, because like I said, the mayor's office, they have control with a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Veterans are treated like dirt in the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: And it's a big problem here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

chapters.title: Morano gives closing remarks and adjourns hearing

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I, again, want to thank Chair Hudson for her partnership and her diligence in this oversight topic and this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as comes as no surprise to any of us that follow his city council career,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I want to especially acknowledge once again Councilmember Wong as being the only non-chair that stays till the very end of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: He is a model public servant.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And if there's any justice in the world, all of his birthday wishes will come true today and always.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I do hope that this is not even close to the end of the discussion of the work that we're doing on veteran homelessness and in looking at a lot of the important legislation that we reviewed today.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Homelessness is a complex problem, veteran homelessness even more so.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I really appreciate where everyone came from today, both physically in some cases and emotionally in others and in terms of their experiential journey.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I think we all want to get to the same place, even if we have a lot of different perspectives as to how to get there.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as long as I have the good fortune of chairing this committee, I'm committed.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: to making sure that we do get there.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So my thanks to the administration, particularly Commissioner Dalton and Commissioner Mata, and my thanks especially to everyone that testified.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And again, I can't stress enough to the public that if you didn't have an opportunity to testify today,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Send us your testimony in writing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It'll absolutely be included in the record.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as the committee prepares a report about today's hearing, it'll absolutely be included as we make decisions about how to pursue different recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You know, one thing that I think is certainly calling out for.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Legislative clarification is when council members can visit Borden Avenue and shelters in general.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I think a lot of my colleagues who may agree on very little all agree that council members have an important oversight role to play, and we'll work to clarify that in terms of legislative language.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: With that, I'm grateful to everyone who attended today's hearing, grateful to everyone who watched, and with that, this hearing is now adjourned.

summary: Joint Committee on Veterans and General Welfare held an oversight hearing on veteran homelessness in New York City, focusing on conditions at the Borden Avenue Veterans Residence and the city's decision to decline a reduced federal VA Grant and Per Diem award.

Administration officials from DVS and DSS testified on housing placements, shelter operations, capital repairs, and funding, while council members pressed on roof leaks, shower privacy, NDAs for shelter visits, food quality, and the loss of federal funds.

Public testimony from veterans, providers, and advocates described both successful housing outcomes and serious concerns about Borden Avenue conditions, oversight access, and the need for greater accountability and investment in veteran services.
